passage.quote:
Orchestration means coordinating several kernels. Its contracts describe reserving
memory, launching kernels, ensuring that inputs are ready before use, keeping
storage alive while needed, and identifying the resulting observable values.

summary: Compose actual completed single-thread kernel runs through persistent live storage, checking device ownership and argument identities at every launch.
Preserve allocation size, untouched storage and lifetime validity across finite serialized chains; released logical identities cannot be revived.
Keep real-runtime completion, visibility, physical allocation and concurrent orchestration as explicit remaining obligations.
remaining: Serialized single-thread, single-arena launch chains and persistent logical storage are proved. Physical runtime completion/visibility and allocation conformance, overlapping or asynchronous launches, multi-arena kernels and general resource guarantees remain unimplemented.

from.quote:
The orchestration layer combines permitted kernel executions while preserving
the assumptions needed for their safety and execution guarantees.

passage.quote:
These guarantees are stated separately, with their required assumptions. For
example, constructing one schedule that finishes does not prove that every
schedule finishes. A stronger progress claim may need a scheduling assumption
that threads are not indefinitely denied execution opportunities.

links.reason: Composition must preserve the premises and meaning of the kernel execution guarantees.
